chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ismail ibn Abd al-Khaliq, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying to Abu Ja'far al-Ahwal, while I was listening: 'Did you go to Basra?' He said, 'Yes'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'How did you see the hastening of the people to this matter and their entering into it?' He said, 'By Allah, they are few, and they have done it but that is little'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is on you to [approach] the juveniles, for they are quickest to every good.'
Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'What are the people of Basra saying regarding this Verse: Say: I do not ask of you any reward for it but love for my near relatives.'

I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, they are saying that it is for the near relatives of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'They lie. But rather it Descended with regards to us especially, regarding the People of the Household, regarding Ali, and Fatima, and Al-Hasan, and Al-Husayn, the ones of the Cloak (peace be upon them all)'.
ai.seo_question: Who are the 'near relatives' mentioned in the verse of Mawaddah?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) refutes the Sunni claim that 'Qurba' refers to the Prophet's general kinship, asserting instead that the verse specifically mandates love for the Ahl al-Bayt, particularly the People of the Cloak. This distinction underscores the Shia doctrine of Imamate and the unique spiritual authority of the Prophet's progeny, linking the verse to the concept of divine appointment (Nass). The narration also highlights the rapid acceptance of this truth by the 'Ahadith' (those with new knowledge) compared to the broader populace.
